newsitem.title: USA: Prudential reports 1996 profit, capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Prudential reports 1996 profit, capital increase.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co of America reported statutory net income of $1 billion in 1996, despite adding more than $500 million to reserves in connection with a class-action lawsuit against it.
In addition, Prudential said it added $684 million to its capital base, bringing its total statutory capital position to $12.1 billion.
Prudential, which was required to switch to a new accounting standard in 1996, said it will issue more detailed results in about a month.

As a result of the switch to a new generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) standard for mutual insurance companies, the 1996 statutory results are not comparable to Prudential's 1995 results, Prudential controller Martin Berkowitz said.
In 1995, Prudential said it earned $579 million in after-tax income and added $1.9 billion to its capital.

Prudential added $410 million to reserves in 1996 for the class-action settlement of deceptive sales practice complaints and added $90 million to reserve for the plaintiffs' attorneys legal fees, Berkowitz said.
Prudential also added $36 million to reserves for the payment of fines included in a settlement with a multistate task force of insurance regulators over deceptive sales practices, Berkowitz said.
Prudential said its 1996 results also were achieved despite disappointing performances from its Prudential Bank and Prudential HealthCare businesses.
The financial performance of both those units was hurt, in part, by adverse industry conditions, Prudential said.
Both units are currently undergoing restructuring, Prudential said.
Contributing to the company's 1996 financial results was the sale of the company's Canadian Branch at a gain of $138 million.

"We made significant progress in resolving our past sales practices issues last year, and we will continue our efforts to provide remedies to policyowners with legitimate claims and to demonstrte our commitment to resolve their concerns," chairman and chief executive Arthur Ryan said.
"Prudential is committed to doing the right thing, and at the same time, we are moving head with the development of new products and services to meet the changing needs of consumers," he said.

Prudential said its board of directors late last year approved the company's 1997 dividend scale, which will result in payouts to policyholders in 1997 of about five percent more than if the 1996 dividend scale had been continued.
The dividend scale increase reflects the company's strong 1996 financial performance and overall solid financial position, the company said.
In 1996, dividends to policyholders totaled $2.5 billion.
"Prudential is well on its way to improving its financial performance," Ryan said. "The last two years clearly show an upward trend of increasing financial strenght."
